{"id":"PKIX-f1j4.13","title":"Every cache check on hit clones the verifier — V: Clone bound forces unnecessary allocation for verifiers carrying state","description":"src/cache.rs:592, 617, 774, 791 (and matching sync sites in crl.rs:85 / ocsp.rs:88): `CrlChecker::new(cached.bytes.as_slice(), self.inner.now_unix, self.inner.verifier.clone())`. The V: SignatureVerifier + Clone bound is propagated through the wrapper.

For verifiers that are zero-cost copies (DefaultVerifier, unit structs), this is free. For verifiers that carry state (a verifier wrapping a hardware key handle, or an Arc<dyn Verifier>), the clone is a refcount bump per check_revocation call. Not a real bottleneck.

But the design choice forces V: Clone on every consumer. A verifier that is naturally not Clone (e.g. holds an &mut to a hardware token) can't be used. Mitigations: (a) take &V in CrlChecker::new (changes pkix-revocation API; pre-1.0 fine), (b) accept Arc<dyn SignatureVerifier> as the canonical shape (breaks generic monomorphization, also fine), or (c) leave as-is and add a docstring note that Clone is required.

Out-of-scope for this crate to change pkix-revocation's CrlChecker::new signature; in-scope to note the implication and decide whether to push the change up to pkix-revocation as part of the 1.0 wave.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-05-14T18:58:19Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-05-14T18:58:19Z","metadata":{},"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"","depends_on_id":"PKIX-f1j4","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-05-14T11:58:19Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

new_value:
Fixed properly, without any of the three options the bead listed.

The bead offered (a) change CrlChecker::new to take &V (breaking, adds a lifetime to a public type across the workspace), (b) make Arc the canonical shape (breaking), or (c) leave it and add a docstring note. It also scoped itself to 'note the implication and decide whether to push the change up'.

There was a fourth option, additive and non-breaking: CrlChecker owns V but every internal use is &self.verifier, so the bound is satisfied by any type that is both SignatureVerifier and Clone -- and a shared reference is Copy. pkix-path now forwards SignatureVerifier through &T (unconditional) and Arc<T> (gated on std). A verifier owning a hardware token handle or an open session is passed as &verifier for a scoped validation, or Arc<verifier> for a fetcher with no borrow to hold. No signature changed anywhere.

The Arc impl is gated on std deliberately: Arc needs alloc::sync, which requires atomic CAS, and pkix-path advertises no_std. Implementing it unconditionally would break a future thumbv6m target silently; the three bare-metal targets in CI happen to have atomics, which is not a reason to depend on it.

Also promoted pkix-path's private 'use spki::{AlgorithmIdentifierRef, SubjectPublicKeyInfoRef}' to a re-export, found while writing the test: both appear in verify_signature's signature, so implementing the trait requires naming them, and they were reachable only by reading pkix-path's source and taking a direct spki dependency. No new coupling -- they were already public API by virtue of being in the signature.

tests/non_clone_verifier.rs is mostly a compile-time assertion: its verifier deliberately omits Clone, so the file stops building if either forwarding impl is removed, and it counts calls to confirm the forwarding reaches the real impl rather than a default. Commits ef1fd31a, a829edc8.
